newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX BRENT TO WEAKEN ON RISE IN API CRUDE STOCKS.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX BRENT TO WEAKEN ON RISE IN API CRUDE STOCKS.

text.p: September Brent futures was unquoted at midday on Wednesday, although prices were assessed weaker in line with the rise in the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) stock levels.
API reported a rise in the U.S crude inventories of 2.7 million barrels, despite earlier expectations of a drawdown.
Although there were no quotes on SIMEX Brent, Singapore brokers expected bids and offers to be lower by 10-20 cents from London overnight.
September Brent on IPE on Tuesday had closed 27 cents per barrel higher at $18.85, boosted by the renewed strength in the U.S. gasoline market.
But brokers said that impact of the bearish API was mitigated by relatively high utilitization rates of U.S. refineries.
"Normally, with that kind of buildup in crude, prices would fall more drastically, by at least 30-40 cents. But I think prices will just weaken a little as utilization rates are high" said a broker.
NYMEX crudes on ACCESS last traded at $19.87, down 12 cents per barrel from New York, following the release of the API data.
